transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got the medical-device housing run scheduled for Thursday, and I understand the virgin polymer we have on hand isn't enough to complete the planned batch. I also know there's a lot of reclaimed polymer pellets sitting in the materials cage that hasn't been authorized for this product yet. Before I make any decision on whether to authorize that reclaimed lot, I need to hear from both quality and environmental compliance. Please state your exact requirements and confirm which controls you'll complete before Thursday's run. Once I have both of your responses on the record, I'll settle the authorization and control plan.

transcript.text: My completed lab review shows the reclaimed polymer is suitable for this housing only at a 15% reclaimed-to-85% virgin blend. I also confirmed that the first 50 molded housings must receive FTIR identity testing, but I want to flag that the lab result has not yet been attached to the production traveler.

transcript.text: I need to put my environmental-compliance requirements on the record. My review of the supplier's revised safety data sheet — received late yesterday and not yet entered in the plant's chemical register — classifies the reclaimed lot's additive residue as regulated process waste. That means we need labeled segregated storage and a hazardous-waste manifest for any discarded pellets or purge material. I can complete the chemical-register entry, storage setup, and manifest procedures before Thursday, and I will provide environmental-compliance sign-off once those controls are complete.
